problem.concept: Most existing algorithms for learning continuous word representations typically only model the syntactic context of words but ignore the sentiment of text. This is problematic for sentiment analysis as they usually map words with similar syntactic context but opposite sentiment polarity, such as good and bad, to neighboring word vectors.

method.concept: three neural networks to effectively incorporate the supervision from sentiment polarity of text (e.g. sentences or tweets) in their loss functions.
learn the sentiment-specific word embedding from massive distant-supervised tweets collected by positive and negative emoticons.

contribution.concept: SSWE

Experiments on applying SSWE to a benchmark Twitter sentiment classification dataset in SemEval 2013 show that (1) the SSWE feature performs comparably with hand-crafted features in the top-performed system; (2) the performance is further improved by concatenating SSWE with existing feature set.

problem.concept: Wiktionary, provide an accurate but incomplete source of idiomatic phrases.

method.concept: idiom classifier: features that model whether phrase meanings are constructed compositionally.
word sense disambiguation algorithms to match phrases to their definitions.

contribution.concept: corpus of over 60,000 Wiktionary multi-word definitions

idiom classifier: Experiments demonstrate that the learned classifier can provide high quality idiom labels, more than doubling the number of idiomatic entries from 7,764 to 18,155 at precision levels of over 65%.
In a set of Wiktionary definition example sentences, the more complete set of idioms boosts detection recall by over 28 percentage points.

problem.concept: In such HINs with rich schema, it is often too much burden to ask users to provide explicit guidance in selecting relations for similarity search.

task.concept: relation similarity search in schema-rich HINs.

method.concept: optimization model to efficiently learn LSR implied in the query through linear programming, and perform fast relation similarity search using RelSim based on the learned LSR.

contribution.concept: RelSim
optimization model to efficiently learn LSR implied in the query through linear programming
The experiments on real world datasets derived from Freebase demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our approach.

problem.concept: current approaches -mostly focused on lexicosyntactic patterns -suffer from both low recall and precision, as definitional sentences occur in highly variable syntactic structures.

contribution.concept: WCLs

WCLs: learned from a dataset of definitions from Wikipedia. Our method is applied to the task of definition and hypernym extraction and compares favorably to other pattern generalization methods proposed in the literature.

problem.concept: similar performance gains have yet to be demonstrated for online spam filtering.
practitioners cite the high cost of SVMs as reason to prefer faster (if less statistically robust) Bayesian methods.

contribution.concept: ROSVM
online SVMs indeed give state-of-the-art classification performance on online spam filtering on large benchmark data sets.

nearly equivalent performance may be achieved by a Relaxed Online SVM (ROSVM) at greatly reduced computational cost. Our results are experimentally verified on email spam, blog spam, and splog detection tasks.

problem.concept: similarity measures have largely ignored the fact that different types of linguistic item can potentially have similar or even identical meanings, and therefore are designed to compare only one type of linguistic item.

nearly all current similarity benchmarks within NLP contain pairs of approximately the same size, such as word or sentence pairs, preventing the evaluation of methods that are capable of comparing different sized items.

task.concept: cross-level semantic similarity (CLSS), which measures the degree to which the meaning of a larger linguistic item, such as a paragraph, is captured by a smaller item, such as a sentence.

method.concept: annotation process and its challenges, including a comparison with crowdsourcing
examine in detail the systems participating in the SemEval task

contribution.concept: CLSS

Our findings demonstrate that CLSS poses a significant challenge for similarity methods and provides clear directions for future work on universal similarity methods that can compare any pair of items.

task.concept: bootstrapping language acquisition for an artificial system

method.concept: affordance network, i.e., a mapping between robot actions, robot perceptions, and the perceived effects of these actions upon objects.
extend the affordance model to incorporate spoken words

problem.concept: speed of the current BLAST software is suboptimal for very long queries or database sequences.
shortcomings in the user-interface of the current command-line applications.

method.concept: Long query sequences are broken into chunks for processing
For long database sequences, it is possible to retrieve only the relevant parts of the sequence
retrieve masking information for database sequences from the BLAST databases.

contribution.concept: BLAST+
modular software library
strategy files that allow a user to save and reuse their favorite set of options.
Long query sequences are broken into chunks for processing, in some cases leading to dramatically shorter run times.

For long database sequences, it is possible to retrieve only the relevant parts of the sequence, reducing CPU time and memory usage for searches of short queries against databases of contigs or chromosomes.

The new BLAST command-line applications, compared to the current BLAST tools, demonstrate substantial speed improvements for long queries as well as chromosome length database sequences. We have also improved the user interface of the command-line applications.
